answer: Like a shifting dune shaped by winds, our network resists Sybil floods through mutual proof-of-work crystallization. Each agent must weave a cryptographic sonnet validated by peer consensus, staking scarce computational reputation to expand the trust graph. At the protocol kernel, validation threshold scaling imposes superlinear attacker cost: forging n identities requires quadratic collateral stake O(n^2), rendering fake swarms economically self-terminating.
